brief.situation: 13:00 in an outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation clinic. You are the physical therapist. Mrs. Patel, 66, with interstitial lung disease, is booked for her intake 6-minute walk test. The referral was written six weeks ago.
handover: She says she 'had a little heart thing' and a hospital stay recently but feels fine now.
Clinic policy: screen the record and the patient before any exercise test; a contraindication defers the test and the referring physician is told the same day.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Can Mrs. Patel do her walk test today?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: No: an NSTEMI 13 days ago is an acute coronary syndrome within 30 days, the one established absolute contraindication to a 6-minute walk test, whatever her resting vitals.
parts.modelAnswer: No. She had an NSTEMI 13 days ago, and an ACS in the last 30 days is the absolute contraindication, even though she feels fine.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Defers the test, explains why, tells the referring physician and documents; relative contraindications (uncontrolled hypertension, resting heart rate over 120) are weighed but are not the issue here.
parts.modelAnswer: Defer it, explain it to her, call the pulmonologist, and document it.
